papers.title: Surgery of retrosternal thyroid: evaluation of 82 cases.
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Retrosternal goiter (RSG) remains one of the most challenging conditions in thyroid surgery because of its variable mediastinal extension, close relationship with vital mediastinal structures, and occasional need for extracervical surgical approaches. Although advances in perioperative management have improved surgical outcomes, contemporary long-term single-center experiences remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, surgical management, postoperative outcomes, and histopathological findings of patients with retrosternal goiter treated over a 13-year period at a tertiary referral center. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed including consecutive patients who underwent surgery for retrosternal goiter at Erciyes University Faculty of Medicine between January 2012 and June 2025. Demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms, thyroid function, operative procedures, postoperative complications, and histopathological findings were retrospectively reviewed. RESULTS: A total of 82 patients were included. The mean age was 55.0 ± 13.0 years, and 59.8% were female. Cervical swelling was the most common presenting symptom, while nearly one-third of patients were diagnosed incidentally. 91% of patients were euthyroid preoperatively. Total thyroidectomy was the predominant surgical procedure. A transcervical approach was sufficient in 80 patients (97.6%); one patient required partial sternotomy for deep anterior mediastinal extension with fibrous adhesions to the brachiocephalic vessels, and one underwent thoracotomy for posterior retroesophageal extension with subcarinal involvement. Temporary hypocalcemia was the most frequent postoperative complication, whereas permanent hypocalcemia and permanent recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy occurred in 3.7% and 1.2% of patients, respectively. papers.title: KNOWLEDGE AND PERCEPTIONS OF FEMALE PELVIC FLOOR DISORDERS AMONG PARTNERED MALES.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the knowledge and perceptions of female pelvic floor disorders (PFDs) among men in active or former long-term relationships. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Men 45 years and older previously or currently in a long-term (≥3 years) intimate relationship with a woman were recruited from a urology clinic. Respondents completed the validated Prolapse and Incontinence Knowledge Questionnaire, with supplemental questions assessing attitudes on PFDs. The primary outcome was knowledge proficiency in the pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and urinary incontinence (UI) domains, defined as ≥50% and >75% correct, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analysis assessed factors associated with proficiency in both domains. Secondary outcomes included rates of high response confidence, defined as responding with "don't know" less than 50% of the time. RESULTS: Of the 134 respondents, 22% demonstrated proficiency in the POP and 13% in the UI domain, with median scores of 1/12 and 3.5/12, respectively. Employed men were more likely to demonstrate knowledge proficiency (POP: aOR 6.24, p <0.01; UI: aOR 6.94, p=0.024) and exhibit higher rates of response confidence (POP: aOR 5.39, p=0.01; UI: aOR 5.54, p<0.01), relative to retired men. Higher education, older age, and having a partner with POP were associated with proficiency in the POP domain only. Fewer than 25% of men felt they should be involved in treatment decisions related to PFD. CONCLUSION: Men in long-term relationships exhibited low PFD knowledge. Future research is needed to determine if a relationship exists between improved knowledge among male partners and care-seeking behavior among women with PFDs.

papers.title: Quality of life in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: positive associations with younger age, higher education, low disease activity, and corticosteroid and cyclophosphamide treatment-cross-sectional study in northwestern Poland.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) - chronic autoimmune disease affecting health-related quality of life (QoL). To estimate the associations between QoL and age, disease activity, education level, and treatment in patients with SLE. We studied 200 SLE patients. Data collected: sex, age, disease duration, socioeconomic status, disease activity, and treatment. QoL was assessed using the Lupus Quality of Life Questionnaire (LupusQoL), 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ). Younger patients reported better QoL (all p < 0.001). Disease duration correlated positively with pain (p = 0.002) and role limitations due to physical health (p = 0.03) in the SF-36. Low SLEDAI correlated positively with QoL in most of the domains assessed by the LupusQoL (all p < 0.05), despite physical health, pain and burden to others, and intimate relationships (all p > 0.05). The use of CS improved physical health (p = 0.01) and physical functioning (p = 0.03) in the LupusQoL and SF-36, respectively. Intravenous cyclophosphamide improved physical health (p = 0.01), oral cyclophosphamide improved intimate relationships (p = 0.003) in the LupusQoL. Secondary and higher education correlated positively with planning (p = 0.007 and p = 0.005, respectively) and intimate relationships (p = 0.0001 and p = 0.0002, respectively) in the LupusQoL and with role limitations due to emotional problems (p = 0.01 and p = 0.007, respectively) in the SF-36. QoL assessment in patients with SLE was positively associated with younger age, higher education, low disease activity, and treatment.

papers.title: A Result-Auditable Protocol for Low-Data Classification of Blue-and-White Porcelain Botanical Motifs Using Frozen Chinese-CLIP Features.
papers.abstract: Low-data visual classification is common in cultural heritage documentation, where expert labels are expensive, and image sources are heterogeneous. This protocol provides result-level audit support for classifying five botanical motifs-peony, lotus, chrysanthemum, plum blossom, and bamboo-on blue-and-white porcelain. It combines operational label definitions, source documentation, perceptual hash screening, and fixed, stratified, image-level splits with a frozen Chinese Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (Chinese-CLIP) Vision Transformer (ViT-L/14-336) visual encoder. A training-only StandardScaler and an L2-regularized multinomial logistic regression classifier form the primary model. In a 259-image demonstration, five overlapping image-level splits yielded 91.28% ± 2.47% accuracy and 91.22% ± 2.44% macro-F1. These are image-level demonstration estimates and may be optimistic because complete artifact identifiers are unavailable; they should not be interpreted as artifact-level, population-level, or confirmatory performance. A retrospective sensitivity analysis that excluded training images linked to test images at a perceptual hash distance ≤15 yielded 91.03% ± 2.03% accuracy. The protocol also specifies few-shot evaluation, metadata controls, feature baselines, prompt sensitivity, and checksum-based archiving. An exploratory assessment of all 60 external images yielded 85.00% accuracy and 85.89% macro-F1 against provisional labels, and 83.33% accuracy and 84.31% macro-F1 against labels from one blinded professor. Six label disagreements remain unadjudicated. A 54-image agreement subset is secondary only. Because the external v2 collection included replacements after model errors were inspected, none of these external results constitutes independent confirmatory validation. The workflow supports expert-reviewed candidate labeling and retrieval, not autonomous attribution, dating, or authentication.

papers.title: Solvent-Mediated Multi-Factor Structural Modulation for Tunable Phosphorescence in Metal-Organic Frameworks.
papers.abstract: Independently controlling phosphorescence dynamics while preserving the intrinsic emissive state is essential for establishing mechanistically clear framework-phosphorescence relationships and rationally developing diverse phosphorescent metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). Yet conventional ligand/metal screening typically alters the emissive center. Herein, a novel solvent-mediated multi-factor structural modulation strategy yields five Zn-based MOFs with tunable dimensionalities (1D, 2D, 3D) from a single metal/ligand system, exhibiting widely tunable phosphorescence lifetimes (12.6-1045.4 ms) and quantum yields (0.2%-16.2%), while retaining broadly similar ligand-centered green emission, allowing kinetic differences to be attributed primarily to coupled structural variations. Single-crystal structures reveal dimensional, terminal-ligand, and guest-confinement variations governing supramolecular interactions and framework rigidity. Theoretical analysis links these factors to distinct excited-state localization, while γ/β descriptors link orbital mixing to intersystem crossing and radiative decay. Among the five structures, strong hydrogen bonding and guest confinement in the guest-containing 2D MOF afford a 1045.4 ms lifetime, whereas semi-chelate coordination and excited-state localization in 1D MOF may favor a 16.2% quantum yield. These color-stable, lifetime-tunable materials enable covert exclusive-OR optical encoding featuring parity-check self-validation and single-bit error correction. This paradigm provides new chemical insights into decoupling phosphorescence dynamics from the intrinsic emissive state, enabling mechanistic elucidation and rational construction of multiscale, tailorable phosphorescent MOF systems.

papers.title: Partnering with people who stutter for transformative teaching and learning in speech-language pathology.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Service user involvement (SUI) in health professional education is associated with a range of benefits including students' increased understanding of person-centred care and enhanced skills underpinning their communication, and increased service user empowerment. Despite this, it remains an unexplored topic in the stuttering literature and there is limited guidance on how to authentically and sustainably embed the involvement of people who stutter within professional training. The purpose of this short communication is to explore the possibilities of SUI in healthcare education and to advance understanding of meaningful involvement of people who stutter in speech-language pathology (SLP) education. METHOD: The benefits, challenges and facilitators of meaningful SUI in healthcare education are summarised. A taxonomy of client involvement in healthcare education is presented and examples pertaining to the involvement of stuttering service users are provided. Practical recommendations are proposed to support SLP educators' increased involvement of people who stutter in their stuttering curricula. CONCLUSIONS: Despite an increasing literature on the range of benefits of SUI and the fundamental right for service users to be included in healthcare education, research on the meaningful involvement of people who stutter (and parents or carers) in the education of speech-language pathologists (SLPs) remains in its infancy. Their sustained involvement can be supported by educators establishing and maintaining trust with stuttering communities alongside educational institutions' commitment through aligned funding and policy support.

papers.title: EquIPP-AT: a framework proposition for examining equity and inclusion in assistive technology assessment.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Assistive technology (AT) assessment shapes access to products, services and supports. Although discussed as a clinical, technical and user-centred process, it has been less systematically examined as an equity and inclusion process. This article proposes EquIPP-AT, a provisional AT-specific adaptation of the Equity and Inclusion in Policy Processes framework. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This first-stage development adapts EquIPP to AT assessment through evidence synthesis and expert judgement, informed by AT service delivery and outcome literature, Critical Disability Studies, epistemic injustice, the capabilities approach, and comparison with EquiFrame and ARISE. Cases from Norway and Brazil and donation-mediated wheelchair provision in Kenya and the Philippines are used illustratively across provision contexts. RESULTS: EquIPP-AT is organised across three analytical levels: assessment governance and rules, assessment practices, and lived experience of assessment. It applies nine equity dimensions: participation and involvement; individual needs and circumstances; accessibility and reasonable adjustments; leadership, governance and accountability; data, evidence and monitoring; organisational commitment and culture; experiential expertise and co-production; communication and influence; and partnership and collaboration. Four contextual axes are identified: structural variation, marginality and precarity, cultural-epistemic difference, and temporality. It applies across professional-led, peer-supported, collaborative, commercial and self-directed assessment routes. CONCLUSION: EquIPP-AT is a provisional analytical framework, not a validated instrument. It supports systematic inquiry into how AT assessment processes include, exclude, recognise, constrain or enable AT users. papers.title: The practical road to elimination of neglected tropical diseases: assessing the past and looking into the future.
papers.abstract: Eliminating neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) is critical for reducing poverty, addressing inequality and achieving universal health coverage. As the World Health Organization 2021-2030 Roadmap enters its second half, 2026 represents a pivotal year for translating decades of implementation gains into sustainable elimination outcomes. These have been through expanded access to preventive chemotherapy (PC), strengthened morbidity management and surveillance systems. In Africa, the population requiring PC decreased from 630 million in 2015 to 518.6 million in 2025 with few diseases eliminated in many countries.   Sustaining these achievements and accelerating progress towards elimination require updated prevalence mapping, impact assessments, post-treatment surveillance and continuous community engagement while targeting persistent transmission hotspots. However, dwindling external financing threatens program sustainability. Hence, domestic financing, stronger political commitment and country ownership must be prioritized, with continued external technical support for strengthening national capacity and resilient health systems. Collaboration with water, sanitation and hygiene, environmental health and vector-control programs remain critical. Emerging zoonotic threats, demographic changes, import restrictions, fragile supply chains, insecurity and other country-specific challenges must be systematically addressed. The NTD community must move from commitments to measurable impact. Integrating NTD interventions into primary healthcare systems offers a cost-effective and sustainable pathway to elimination.

papers.title: Human Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Neuromyocardial Organoids for Modeling Cardiomyocyte Development and Recovery from Hypoxia/Reoxygenation Injury.
papers.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived organoids have emerged as powerful platforms for modeling human development, disease, and injury responses in vitro. Here, we describe a robust, scalable, and cost-effective protocol for generating neuromyocardial organoids (NMOs) from hiPSCs cultured in three-dimensional (3D) conditions. The protocol combines suspension-based hiPSC maintenance with a stepwise differentiation strategy using chemically defined media formulations to reproducibly co-specify neural and myocardial derivatives within the same organoid. Notably, the protocol relies exclusively on chemically defined, animal-free media and standard, low-cost tissue-culture plasticware, avoiding the ultra-low-attachment plates, anti-adherence coatings, and extracellular matrices required by many existing organoid systems. The resulting NMOs exhibit spontaneous contractile activity by day 6 and achieve >90% beating efficiency by day 7; they contain multiple cell populations relevant to embryonic development, including cardiomyocytes, neural cells, endothelial cells, and smooth muscle cells. To demonstrate the utility of this organoid platform for injury studies, we further establish a hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) injury model in mature (≥30 day), spontaneously beating NMOs. Live Hoechst/Propidium iodide (PI) staining enables longitudinal monitoring of injury-induced cell death in the same organoids, minimizing inter-sample variability. In parallel, real-time oxygen consumption rate (OCR) measurements using a real-time OCR monitoring system allow non-invasive assessment of metabolic and respiratory recovery following injury. Together, this protocol provides an accessible and reproducible platform for studying human multi-lineage tissue development, multicellular cardiac-neural interactions, hypoxic injury, and post-injury metabolic recovery in vitro.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of clinical findings in women injured by blunt trauma resulting from intimate partner violence and non-intimate partner violence.
papers.journal: Journal of forensic and legal medicine
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Violence against women frequently manifests as physical assault, with blunt trauma being the most common type. This study aims to compare the clinical features and assault characteristics among women who experienced blunt trauma resulting from intimate partner violence (IPV) and non-intimate partner violence (non-IPV), thereby contributing to efforts to prevent recurrent violence. METHODS: This retrospective study included 420 female patients aged 15 years or older who sustained blunt trauma because of physical violence between 2016 and 2025. Data were extracted from the Hafsa Sultan Hospital information system and summarized descriptively. The tabulated categorical analyses were verified using Pearson chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Monte Carlo multinomial tests. RESULTS: IPV accounted for 75.0% of cases (315/420), while 25.0% were non-IPV (105/420). Among IPV cases, 67.0% were assaulted by husbands, 18.1% by boyfriends, and 14.9% by former partners. Among non-IPV cases, 71.4% were assaulted by individuals known to the victim. Facial lesions accounted for 32.0% of all recorded lesions. Fractures were identified in 46 women (11.0%), with 56 fractures recorded. Among facial fractures in the IPV group, 52.6% were nasal fractures. Previous hospital admissions for trauma were documented in 6.7% of IPV cases and 1.9% of non-IPV cases. Pregnancy at the time of violence was documented in 5.4% and 2.9% of IPV and non-IPV cases, respectively. The difference in fracture occurrence was not statistically significant (P = 0.207). Facial lesion proportions were similar between groups (P = 0.795), while abdominal lesions represented a larger proportion of non-IPV than IPV lesion records (11.6% versus 6.2%; P = 0.019); lesion-level tests assumed independent records and were exploratory. papers.title: A scoping review evaluating artificial intelligence applications across various injury prevention domains.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly utilized for injury prevention across diverse clinical and community settings including machine learning (ML). This scoping review aimed to synthesize the current literature on the applications and predictive performance of AI across multiple injury prevention domains. METHODS: This scoping review searched five major databases, including PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, and the Cochrane Library, to identify studies evaluating AI applications for injury prevention published through May 2026. Eligible studies included original U.S.-based, English-language research across self-harm and suicide, abuse and violence, fall prevention, and sports injury prediction. Studies were excluded if they lacked measurable prevention outcomes or sufficient methodological detail, or focused on injury treatment rather than prevention, to ensure relevant and interpretable evidence for synthesis. RESULTS: Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. ML models generally outperformed or matched traditional screening methods for self-harm and suicide prediction (AUC 0.81-0.82), while multimodal approaches achieved the highest predictive accuracy (AUC 0.90). In abuse and violence prevention, AI predicted intimate partner violence with an AUC of 0.88 and identified cases before formal disclosure. AI also improved fall risk assessment by accurately categorizing patient risk levels, predicting future falls, and mitigating fall injuries through wearable airbag technology. ML models predicted future sports-related injuries (AUC 0.76-0.84), while identifying modifiable risk factors including workload, strength deficits, prior injury burden, and concussion history. CONCLUSION: ML-based prediction showed promise for risk stratification in self-harm, suicide, intimate partner violence, and recurrent victimization. papers.title: Youth exposures to family violence and technology-facilitated sexual violence: The mediating role of online help-seeking.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Technology-facilitated sexual violence (TFSV) is increasingly prevalent among youth. Research has identified associations between offline child maltreatment (CM) and TFSV, though associations between youth exposure to intimate partner violence (IPV) between adults in the home and TFSV have not been reported. Youth often turn to the internet for support when dealing with offline harm. Online help-seeking behaviors in the context of offline violence have not been explored as a potential risk factor for TFSV experiences among youth. OBJECTIVE: To assess the relationship between family violence (i.e., CM and/or IPV) exposure and youth's experiences of TFSV and determine whether online help-seeking mediates the relationship between family violence and TFSV. PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: Participants (n = 1877 19- and 20-year-olds in the U.S.) reported on their life experiences during high school (before age 18). Half of participants (n = 946, 50%) reported no family violence history; others reported exposure to IPV only (9%, n = 178), CM only (12%, n = 216), and both IPV and CM (29%, n = 537). METHODS: Data were collected online through Dynata in 2025. Survey items included demographics, family violence histories, TFSV experiences, and online help-seeking behaviors. Structural equation modeling with covariates and Monte Carlo confidence intervals to assess mediation effects tested whether online help-seeking mediated the relationship between family violence exposure and TFSV. RESULTS: Participants exposed to family violence reported significantly higher online help-seeking rates than participants without victimization histories (χ2(N = 1877) =76.62, p < .001). papers.title: Promoting resilience in primary caregivers of people with dementia through health programmes: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Given dementia's global public health impact and the substantial burden borne by family caregivers, there is a need to shift from deficit-focused models towards understanding and promoting caregiver resilience as a dynamic protective process. OBJECTIVE: To synthesise the available evidence on the influence of support programmes on resilience among family caregivers of people with dementia. INFORMATION SOURCES: Four electronic databases (WoS, Scopus, PubMed y CINAHL) covering peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2025. METHODS: A systematic review was reported in accord with the PRISMA reporting guidelines and a PROSPERO-registered protocol, independent study selection and data extraction, quality appraisal using JBI tools, and a narrative synthesis of findings applying the SWiM approach and thematic analysis. RESULTS: A total of 21 studies published between 2015 and 2025 were included. The intervention studies evaluated mindfulness-based, psychoeducational, counselling, cognitive-behavioural, arts-based, and peer-support programmes. Several studies reported improvements in resilience or related caregiver outcomes, including burden, psychological distress, coping, and quality of life, although results varied across interventions and study designs. Complementary observational, qualitative, and measurement evidence identified self-efficacy, adaptive coping, social support, and relationship quality as mechanisms relevant to programme influence, whereas behavioural and neuropsychiatric symptoms of the person with dementia were associated with lower resilience. Sustained follow-up appeared relevant to maintaining programme-related benefits. CONCLUSIONS: Support programmes may strengthen resilience and improve related health and well-being outcomes among family caregivers of people with dementia, particularly when they include psychoeducational, counselling, mindfulness-based, or sustained follow-up components. papers.title: Adolescents During the Pandemic: Supportive and In-Person Rather Than Digital Social Connections Are Associated With Lower Sadness.
papers.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Social connections support emotional well-being and act as buffer against depression during challenging life episodes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, adolescent's social connectedness was disrupted. Here, we examined the association between social connectedness and sadness in a large US sample of adolescents during the pandemic. METHODS: As part of the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development Study, adolescents completed two online surveys around May (n = 5,298, mage: 12.5 years, 49.7% female) and August 2020 (n = 5,051, mage: 12.7, 49.0% female), including the National Institute of Health Toolbox Sadness Questionnaire short form, and questions about relationship quality, parent-child engagement, and digital connections. Mixed linear models tested associations between social connection and sadness with time points as covariate, sadness was compared between clusters sharing social characteristics. RESULTS: In independent models, household conflicts were associated with higher sadness (p < .01), whereas positive parent-child engagement and relationships, such as having dinner together and talking with parents about plans, were associated with lower sadness (p < .01). Texting, social media, and video chat time were associated with greater sadness (p < .01). Clusters with lower digital communications, stronger parent-child engagement, and better relationships, showed the lowest sadness score. Shifting to less digital connections from May to August was associated with a stronger sadness decrease (p < .01). DISCUSSION: In-person, rather than digital, and nonconflictual social connections were associated with lower sadness in adolescents in the pandemic context, emphasizing differences between proximal and remote social connections, and possible emotional costs of over-reliance on remote, digital forms of interaction.
